subject: Oakbridge: end-to-end tail targets + streaming concurrency — post-demo next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam Jenkins <liam.jenkins@oakbridge.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2024 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Oakbridge: end-to-end tail targets + streaming concurrency — post-demo next steps

Thanks again for the demo time this morning, Liam — appreciate the context on the contact-center routing workload. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have an aligned plan for a hosted POC: 

Summary of Oakbridge targets (from the call)
- Primary goal: match or beat incumbent perceived latency – you called out target windows of p95 ~220ms and p99 ~430ms end-to-end for the short-turn prompts used in routing decisions.
- Streaming: persistent streaming connections for partial transcripts; expected sustained concurrent streams: 180-260 during peak, spiking to ~340 during campaign bursts.
- Throughput envelope: baseline 350 requests/s, peak sustained 600 req/s for 10-15 minute windows during batch loads.
- Token characteristics: median request ~45 tokens input, median generated output ~120 tokens; prefix reuse high for consecutive messages within sessions.

What Redwood will do next (proposed)
1) Run hosted POC against a traffic envelope derived from your sample traces. Well stage two phases: baseline (synthetic replay matching median token sizes) and burst (simulate the 10-15m peak).
2) Validate p95/p99 E2E (HTTP-level) at the gateway + streaming tail for partial-response latency. Well capture both token-emission latency and final response time.
3) Provide a short canary config for streaming concurrency (connection pooling, keepalive, heartbeat cadence) and recommended client backoff.
4) Deliver a results packet (CSV + traces) and a short ops-runbook with recommended routing/fallback knobs.

Ask from you
- Confirm that the p95/p99 windows above match what you expect (or provide numbers we should treat as the SLO bar).
- Share a sanitized sample trace if available (headers removed) so we can tune replay. If youre okay, attach to reply or we can use the CSV I sent attached.
- Any constraints on test timing (blackout windows, procurement hold-ups) we should be aware of.

I attached: oakbridge_traffic_profile_v2.csv (traffic envelope summary we captured from the call).

Proposed schedule
- Kickoff replay + baseline run: next Tue (4/9) morning PT
- Burst simulation + streaming validation: 4/10 afternoon PT
- Results packet and follow-up sync: 4/11 or 4/12

If that works well schedule the runs and share the lightweight runbook ahead of the baseline.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: oakbridge_traffic_profile_v2.csv
From: Liam Jenkins <liam.jenkins@oakbridge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@oakbridge.com
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2024 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Oakbridge: end-to-end tail targets + streaming concurrency — post-demo next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The p95/p99 bands you listed are the internal targets were trying to achieve in production. Historically our incumbent averages p95 ~260ms and p99 ~520ms when measured end-to-end (we often see variability when downstream routing and tokenization add overhead). Were asking vendors to demonstrate consistent improvement of at least 10-15% at p95 under our traffic envelope.
- Streaming: heartbeat cadence is 15s for client keepalive; payloads are small per-chunk (avg 8-12 tokens/chunk) but were sensitive to initial chunk latency since that affects perceived responsiveness in the agent UI.
- Blackouts: avoid heavy testing 4/8 (internal maintenance window) and early mornings PT 4/11 (billing cycle close).

I attached a sanitized trace snippet (oakbridge_trace_snippet.json) that strips user identifiers but preserves timing and chunk sizes. Use it for replay and let me know if you need an expanded sample set.

On procurement: procurement@oakbridge.com is looped for visibility. They asked that POC artifacts be in a shared Drive folder and that any proposed commitment/discount terms reference deal HB-2024-0381.

I'll confirm offline whether we can widen the peak window to 800 req/s for a single 5-minute spike; that would help test autoscaling behavior.

-Liam
Liam Jenkins
Senior Engineering Manager, Oakbridge Health
liam.jenkins@oakbridge.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam Jenkins <liam.jenkins@oakbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2024 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Oakbridge: end-to-end tail targets + streaming concurrency — post-demo next steps

Nice recap. I put together a concise probe plan and a runnable script we can use in the hosted environment. Key notes: 

- Probe approach: two-stage replay (baseline + burst) using the attached script. The script can drive streaming sessions (WebSocket/HTTP2) and measure per-chunk latency and final-response latency.
- Metrics captured: per-request start->first-token, per-request start->end-of-response, per-chunk inter-arrival, connection churn rate, error counts (429/503), and CPU/GPU utilization snapshots from the Redwood runtime.
- Acceptance criteria (initial): p95 <= 240ms, p99 <= 480ms for baseline traffic. If we meet that under your envelope, well iterate to target the 10-15% improvement you requested.

Proposed probe window: run baseline replay 4/9 09:00-11:00 PT; run burst + spike 4/10 14:00-15:00 PT. Results CSV will be uploaded immediately after each run.

I attached: latency_probe_script.sh and latency_probe_results_template.csv (template we use to surface the CSV).

Next step: Marissa, want me to fire the baseline on 4/9 once Liam confirms the green window?

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam Jenkins <liam.jenkins@oakbridge.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Apr 2024 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Oakbridge: end-to-end tail targets + streaming concurrency — post-demo next steps

Thanks Ben. Liam Benhas the script and will coordinate run times with your ops contact. Confirmations:
- Well avoid 4/8 and early 4/11 per your blackout notes.
- Baseline run scheduled: 4/9 09:00 PT. Burst + potential spike (800 req/s for 5m) pending your confirmation; if you approve well run the spike during the 4/10 window.
- Deliverables: post-run CSV + zipped traces + short ops-runbook (recommended keepalive 20s for clients, client-side jitter on reconnects, and fallback to smaller model variant on sustained p99 > threshold).

Ive added the HubSpot deal link to our internal notes: https://hubspot.example/deal/HB-2024-0381. Ben will upload results to the shared Drive folder you requested after each run.

Action: Liam, can procurement confirm the Drive folder write access? If yes well proceed to schedule and run.

-Marissa
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>

Locking this in on our side. Ive added the baseline run to the Redwood infra calendar and reserved the probe slot. Ben please confirm the script has logging to the results template and that artifacts will be available in: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3Oakbridge-POC-assets
